narrative:
The model determined that you have a 29% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly shaped this outcome were the purpose of the loan, the status of your checking account, and the length of time you have lived at your current residence. The fact that you are requesting the money for business purposes was the single biggest reason the model leaned toward denial. Among approved applicants, only 8.7% use loans for business; most successful applications are for everyday items like radios, TVs, or cars. This made your application stand out as higher risk.

Your checking account balance falling in the 0-200 DM range also pushed the prediction toward bad credit. While many approved customers have no checking account at all, the model viewed your modest positive balance as less reassuring than the accounts of those who were approved.

Living at your present address for four years worked in your favor and pulled the prediction back toward approval. Most approved borrowers have lived in their homes for only about three years, so your stability here helped your case.

To improve your chances next time, consider applying for a smaller loan intended for personal consumption rather than business, or wait until your checking account shows a stronger balance. These changes would directly address the main concerns that led to the current denial. (248 words)
